title: Random forest predicts 6-month unplanned hospitalization in long-term care residents
summary: A random forest using 11 routine-assessment predictors was built for 768 residents of 15 long-term care facilities in Anhui, China, of whom 253 (32.9%) had an unplanned hospitalization within 6 months. AUCs were 0.934 in a held-out test set, 0.953 and 0.869 in two external cohorts. Calibration varied across settings, the study is retrospective and from one province, and prospective implementation is still needed.
ai_technology: Random forest among five machine-learning algorithms on routine long-term care assessment data

evidence.tested: Discrimination, calibration and decision-curve net benefit were assessed in internal and two institutionally distinct external cohorts.
evidence.unknown: Prospective performance, calibration in other regions and effects on care are unknown. Abstract-based; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A random forest ranked residents by risk of hospitalization from 11 routinely collected variables.
